parts.label: (a)
parts.text: By reference to heat effect, explain what is meant by the *root-mean-square* (*r.m.s.*) value of an alternating current.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The variations with time *t* of two currents *I*₁ and *I*₂ are shown in Fig. 10.1 and Fig. 10.2.

[[fig:f1]]

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Use Fig. 10.1 to determine the peak value and the r.m.s. value of the current *I*₁.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 10.2 to determine the peak value and the r.m.s. value of the current *I*₂.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The variation with time *t* of the supply voltage *V* to a house is given by the expression

*V* = 240 sin *kt*

where *V* is in volts, *t* is in seconds and *k* is a constant with unit rad s⁻¹.
parts.text:
The frequency of the supply voltage is 50 Hz.

Determine *k* to two significant figures.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The supply voltage is applied to a heater. The mean power of the heater is 3.2 kW.

Calculate the resistance of the heater.
